Subject: Lighthouse Health - follow-up & items from today's demo

Thanks again for taking the demo today — great conversation. Per request, summarizing the key technical items we covered and the outstanding questions so your engineering and procurement teams can triage. TL;DR: Redwood can support your initial POC with a sandbox dedicated instance, SDK-based auth, and a routing policy that prioritizes latency for triage endpoints and cost for batch embedding jobs.

What we covered (high level):
- SDK setup: client libraries available in Node/Python with built-in retry/backoff and async streaming handlers.
- Auth: API keys for sandbox; recommend mTLS + short-lived tokens (or your OKTA SAML exchange) for production Private deployment.
- Routing: model routing by policy — you can define latency-first routes for real-time triage, cost-first for bulk processing, and region affinity for PHI-sensitive traffic.
- Structured output & tool calling: function calling support + JSON schema enforcement for your discharge summary extractor.
- Embeddings & reranker: can host both embedding model and a lightweight reranker; we also support hybrid reranker hooks so you can keep an internal scoring script.

Outstanding technical questions you flagged:
1) Exact SDK auth flow for our SSO + HSM keywrap.
2) How model fallback chains behave when a preferred model hits concurrency limits (e.g., do short requests get fast-fail or queue?).
3) Cost cap controls per route and token-level cost visibility for dev vs prod.
4) How to wire structured output validation into the response pipeline (fail-fast vs best-effort).

Next steps proposed:
- Marcus: draft a short architecture note that maps Lighthouse endpoints to Redwood routes (latency tier, cost tier, region) — target by Thu EOD.
- Irene & Vanessa: schedule a 60-min technical sync with your platform engineers next week to walk SSO and KMS integration (proposal slots: Wed/Thu mornings PST).
- Lighthouse: share a minimally redacted sample payload and list of required structured fields for the function-calling schema.

Attachments: Lighthouse_Health_Security_Summary.pdf (pdf), proposal-lhf-v1.docx (docx)

Regards,
Irene
Irene Choi
Enterprise Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks Daniel — wrote up a short architecture mapping and answers to the items Asha flagged. High level decisions + config recommendations below. If useful I can convert this to a one-pager and add to the shared Drive.

1) SDK & Auth- Flow: recommended pattern for your SSO + internal STS:
   - Client app exchanges Okta assertion for a short-lived Lighthouse JWT (valid 5m) via internal STS.
   - Redwood SDK accepts the Lighthouse JWT and performs an introspect call to your token endpoint (or validates signed JWTs).
   - For Private deployments we recommend mutual TLS between your VPC and Redwood's ingress; keys stored in your HSM and rotating via our KMS integration.
   - Token lifetime: 5 minutes recommended for high-sensitivity flows; SDK refresh window: refresh if <60s to expiry.

2) Model routing + fallback chains- Proposed routing policy terms to configure in Redwood Console / API:
   - Route: clinician-realtime-us-west
     - policy: latency_primary
     - preferred_models: [model-latency-1, model-latency-2]
     - fallback_chain: [model-latency-2, model-small-cost]
     - concurrency_threshold: 40 per-instance
     - latency_slo_ms: 200
     - fast_fail_on_slo_breach: true (returns explicit fallback token so UI can show offline hint)

   - Route: async-embeddings-batch
     - policy: cost_primary
     - preferred_models: [embed-large-v1]
     - fallback_chain: [embed-quantized-v1]
     - batch_window_sec: 300
     - max_token_cost_per_job: 40.00

   - Region routing: add route metadata region:us-west-2 or region:eu-central-1 and set affinity rules. For PHI fields, add a request tag (e.g., request.tags: ["phi"]) that maps to region-preserving routes and denies cross-region fallback unless explicitly allowed.

3) Structured output & tool calling- Validation modes:
   - fail_strict: reject responses that don't meet JSON schema (recommended for billing/exact extraction).
   - best_effort: attempt to coerce and attach validation errors (recommended for exploratory UX).
   - We can plug a validation webhook in the response pipeline so your downstream services get a validation result + original text.

4) Embeddings & vector storage- Hybrid model:
   - Redwood serves the embedding model in your dedicated pool; vector persistence can remain in your VPC via our connector (we ship Kafka/HTTPS ingestion stubs).
   - Access controls: fine-grained ACLs on ingestion topics + per-route encryption-in-transit.

Operational controls / Observability- token-level cost breakdown, per-request latency traces, and an alert rule template for queue depth that triggers an automatic temporary routing change (e.g., move clinician-realtime to a higher-capacity pool).

Next steps (action owners & timing):
- Marcus: produce a one-pager (arch note + JSON examples for route config) — ETA Thu 2028-01-12 COB.
- Irene: coordinate tech sync and invite Lighthouse infra (target next Tue 08:30 PST).
- Vanessa: prepare SOW skeleton and security evidence checklist for procurement.

Happy to tweak the fallback thresholds — want to align on acceptable latency SLOs for clinician UX before we lock policy defaults.

Cheers,
Marcus
